page_objective: Define how SIPANEL creates SEO content that ranks, supports technical authority, preserves engineering credibility, and converts qualified industrial leads across sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and industrial envelope systems.

seo_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL SEO content must serve real industrial envelope search intent through engineering clarity, technical proof, and conversion-focused structure.
core_principles: Use one primary keyword per page
Represent all core systems: sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and envelope engineering

primary_keyword_rules: Each page must target one primary keyword.
Support multiple industrial envelope system categories.
Include cladding, façade, and standing seam terminology.
Separate roofing keywords from façade keywords.
Target both engineering and installation intent.
Do not make all SEO content sandwich-panel-only.
Use industrial envelope terminology when the page covers multiple systems.

sandwich_panel_keywords: PU vs PIR vs Rockwool panels

rules: Explain the problem before presenting the solution.
Use technical examples where possible.
Include internal links to services, projects, resources, and articles.
Place CTA after value and proof.
Match technical examples to the system category: sandwich panel, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, or envelope engineering.
Avoid forcing waterproofing language onto façade or cladding pages when not relevant.

seo_hero: Relevant system category: sandwich panel, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, or envelope engineering
problem_context: Connection to cost, leakage, delay, waste, thermal movement, façade alignment, wind-load coordination, or execution risk
technical_proof: Diagram, shop drawing, façade section, standing seam detail, or cladding attachment preview

sandwich_panel_topics: PU vs PIR vs Rockwool panels

rules: Include primary keyword.

system_linking_rules: Sandwich panel pages should link to shop drawing, installation, waterproofing, and relevant case studies.
Aluminum cladding pages should link to façade detailing, cladding case studies, and envelope coordination pages.

Envelope engineering pages should link to sandwich panel, cladding, ZIP roofing, and RFQ pages.
